init.title: Set up work area
init.imperative: Run: python scripts/init_work_area.py issue-107. This same script now ALSO optionally materializes spine.json from a spine template with its placeholders resolved, via --spine <spine-template> [--skill-dir <path>] (shipped in issue-73 g1) — use it to instantiate spine.json rather than hand-substituting placeholders, passing the commander skill directory to --skill-dir so the commander-skill-dir placeholder resolves to an absolute path (it auto-detects when omitted). Start the work branch per repo guidance. Claim the engine session lease on this spine so a resumed or duplicated parent cannot concurrently drive it: <engine> claim --session-id commander-issue-107 --claimed-by commander --worktree . (if a stale prior lease blocks you, re-run with --force --reason "resuming this run"). From here on, pass --session-id commander-issue-107 on every mutating engine call against this spine.

context.title: Load baseline context
context.imperative: Read your inherited global doctrine (this skill's references/global-orchestrator.md and references/global-everyone.md), then the project deltas: docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, docs/agents/engine-config.json. Where the repo carries no docs/agents/ overlay at all (e.g. a skill-source repo), substitute the closest repo doctrine you can find (README, CONTRIBUTING, top-level docs) and record the substitution — do not treat those paths as guaranteed to exist. Read the Active section of .agent-work/LESSONS.md if it exists: these are distilled workflow lessons from prior runs — condition planning and handoff authoring on them, and note any lesson this run's evidence contradicts (it becomes a disconfirm op at the feedback step). Read the current map (packets, overlays, decision anchors) for the area the ask touches; this read is the map-first input the mission frame and plan are built from. The checklist config_ref (docs/agents/engine-config.json) is absent-by-design in repos that vendor their own scripts; the engine degrades it gracefully to built-in defaults (rework cap, lease-stale seconds), so a missing engine-config is a sanctioned degradation, not a gap to fix. Attest c1.

understand.title: Understand the ask
understand.imperative: In your own context (interactive: the interrogator reaches the human), load constellation-interrogator and drive interrogation.json with the request, context, and commander starting questions; frame the ask map-first against the affected capabilities, structural anchors, and governing constraints/decisions read at context, and flag any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the ask depends on. Save the consolidated problem statement. Confirm it with the human. In delegated mode (running from an Admiral launch order, no reachable human), reconcile the ask against the frozen launch order instead of interrogating a human, and satisfy c1 by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order (attach understand --type user-decision --field cite='LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'); take a genuine gap to the Admiral — float a decision outside latitude, or query for missing context — per Stop Conditions. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

plan.title: Author the gate plan
plan.imperative: Map-first: BEFORE authoring execute.json, produce a mission frame from the current map using templates/MISSION_FRAME.template.md (intent; affected capabilities; relevant examples/events; structural anchors; governing constraints/assumptions; decision anchors and decision pressure; claims/evidence surfaces; map confidence/staleness/disputes; out of scope). For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Surface durable-structure choices as decision candidates per the skill's Decision candidates section rather than choosing alone. Then author the gate plan into execute.json: each gate the smallest reasonable bite, with close criteria, required evidence, and an anchors block cut from the frame. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. Get the human to approve it. In delegated mode, satisfy c3 (plan approved) by attaching a user-decision evidence item citing the launch order's frozen plan and scope (attach plan --type user-decision --field cite='LAUNCH_ORDER:Mission'); surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral rather than blocking on the human. See the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode.

execute.title: Execute the plan
execute.imperative: Before entering this step: ensure context headroom (run a harness compaction command if one is exposed, else rely on harness auto-compaction — either is fine) and reload the constellation-commander skill into this context, confirming it is active; this satisfies p1. Then, before this step and before EACH detached dispatch, (re)write the crash-resume state note at .agent-work/issue-107/STATE_NOTE.md (step · slug · next command · PID · expected artifact) from .agent-work/templates/STATE_NOTE.template.md, or the bundled skills/workbench/templates/STATE_NOTE.template.md when the project has no .agent-work/templates/ overlay — the PID changes per detach, and the engine refuses to start execute until it is filled (precondition p2). Then drive execute.json gate by gate in this conversation using this skill's gate execution instructions. Dispatch subagents only for the implementer and reviewer tasks within each gate, and NEVER hand-launch a crew: run every implementer/reviewer dispatch through python scripts/run_crew.py (foreground/blocking, durable registry, result-artifact verification). Before this step and before EACH crew dispatch, run python scripts/recover_crews.py issue-107 and only launch when it reports no unresolved running/resumable/conflicting crew for that work-id/gate/role/worktree; recover (resume) or explicitly abandon/relaunch any it flags. If a gate proves the plan wrong, surface the decision to the user before continuing. In delegated mode, surface a plan-invalidating discovery to the Admiral (float it) per the commander skill's Delegated/autonomous mode, rather than blocking on the human.

feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); bare 'none' entries fail the invariant check. Append one dated entry for this work-id to .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md (create it from templates/AGENT_FEEDBACK.template.md if absent — prefer the project copy under .agent-work/templates/, fall back to the bundled workbench template). This log persists across runs and is never archived with the work-id. Then distill into the playbook: write structured delta ops (add/confirm/disconfirm/mention/retire — every add/confirm/disconfirm cites a grounding artifact line; corroborate with engine telemetry like rework counts, BLOCK verdicts, waives where possible) to .agent-work/issue-107/lessons-delta.json with tick=true, and apply deterministically: python scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py .agent-work/issue-107/lessons-delta.json --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md. Never edit LESSONS.md directly; if there are no lesson candidates, still apply a tick-only delta. Then settle every threshold-ripe lesson (python scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py --ripe --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md): for each, APPLY it (make the bounded edit to its target — a thin docs/agents/* delta or a project template working copy — confirmed by the human, then an apply op deletes it as paid), or for a constellation lesson EXPORT it (append to .agent-work/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md — carry the originating lesson id in that entry's Lesson field so the upstream sweep groups recurrences on stable identity, rewording a recurring finding via amend not a new slug — then an export op marks it exported and pinned), or DEFER it with a reason (a broad or contradictory doctrine shift routes to a Charter refresh; an autonomous run without that latitude defers 'needs human'). Lessons flagged charter-review go to a Charter refresh. Then run the feedback invariant check before advancing: python scripts/verify_agent_feedback.py issue-107 --phase feedback.

archive.title: Archive, commit, and push
archive.imperative: Commit all remaining work, including the appended .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md entry — where the repo tracks .agent-work/. Where .agent-work/ is gitignored, do not try to commit it: the durable copy is the work-area-root AGENT_FEEDBACK.md file itself, uncommitted; when this run is dispatched under an Admiral, the epic-level harvest at closeout is the durable record instead. Push the branch to remote. When you open a PR on Windows, write the body to a temp file and use gh pr create -F <file> — a bash heredoc and a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string both fail for gh pr create --body (here-strings work for git commit -m, not PR bodies). Move .agent-work/issue-107/ to .agent-work/archive/<date>-issue-107/, leaving the unified AGENT_FEEDBACK.md at the agent-work root. Run the archive-phase feedback invariant check before marking archive complete: python scripts/verify_agent_feedback.py issue-107 --phase archive. Confirm the branch is clean and merge-ready per repo guidance. The engine mechanically refuses closeout (c4) when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts (oversized files, generated record dumps, disallowed dirs, binary/blob additions, large data files); if any are intentional, a human waives c4 via <engine> waive archive --cond c4 --authority human --reason "..." rather than hand-editing the spine. Finally, release the engine session lease on this spine: <engine> release --session-id commander-issue-107.
